title: GitHub install check in build-wheel.yml uses commit-pinned codeload tarballs, not git+ URLs
answers: How do I test that the built wheel installs from a GitHub commit in CI?
Why does the build-wheel GitHub installation step take so long or time out?
Can I use a git+https requirement in the wheel installation check?
body:
Convention: the post-build GitHub installation check in .github/workflows/build-wheel.yml pins the tested commit with REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD) and installs from https://github.com/${REPO}/archive/${REF}.tar.gz, not a git+https:// requirement.
Reason (from the PR): uv fetches the full Git history for git+ requirements, which made the step slow (33-43s) and exposed it to transient Git backend failures. The tarball step runs in about 19-30s.
Do not switch the check back to git+ URLs. Keep the per-attempt `timeout -k 10 120` and the 3-attempt retry loop around `uv run --isolated --no-project --with "$URL"`.
The check must keep testing the exact commit that built the wheel, so the ref must come from the checked-out HEAD, not a branch name.
applies: Applies to the GitHub installation test step in .github/workflows/build-wheel.yml; not to PyPI-based install tests.
says: The wheel build workflow takes too long during the installation verification step.
Package installation tests in the release pipeline are timing out intermittently.
Speed up the continuous integration step that verifies installation from a commit archive.
Make package install verification faster and resilient against repository connection dropouts in build checks.
